summary: Official NZ election results land at 2pm today, with almost 400,000 special votes able to shift a seat or two and decide whether the National, ACT and NZ First majority holds.

Wall Street clawed back steep losses on Wednesday to finish mixed, with the Dow up 0.3% after being down more than 1,100 points, while Nvidia fell another 3.9%; US markets were shut Thursday for Thanksgiving.
The NZX 50 slipped 0.4% as power companies and Mainfreight fell on tariff worries, while the ASX 200 rebounded 0.8% on a miners' rally.

stories.headline: Wall Street stages a late comeback before Thanksgiving
stories.summary: US stocks recovered most of a sharp sell-off on Wednesday, with the Dow finishing up 0.33% after being down more than 1,100 points, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq closed only modestly lower. Sticky core inflation, renewed tariff worries and weakness in AI stocks drove the early fall, and Nvidia ended down 3.9% after S&P Global Ratings warned of a possible downgrade.
stories.why: Big intraday swings like this show how quickly sentiment can turn, which matters for the global share funds inside most KiwiSaver accounts.

stories.headline: NZX 50 slips as power companies and Mainfreight fall
stories.summary: The NZX 50 fell 0.4% to 13,986.6 on Thursday, with 32 stocks down and 13 up, as Meridian, Mercury and Contact led the losses. Meridian dropped 1.4% after buying an 11% stake in data-centre firm Datagrid for US$30 million, and Mainfreight fell 1.1% amid new US tariffs.
stories.why: Electricity retailers and data centres are a growing story in NZ, and power prices flow straight into running costs for every small business.

nz_politics.headline: Official election results due at 2pm today
nz_politics.summary: The Electoral Commission releases the final count this afternoon, including almost 400,000 special votes, which in recent elections have usually moved a seat or two. Scenarios range from National, ACT and NZ First keeping their slim majority in a 131-seat Parliament, to Opportunity becoming kingmaker or a 65-65 split if the House shrinks to 130 seats.
nz_politics.why: The final seat count decides who forms the next government and therefore the direction of tax, student and small-business policy.

nz_politics.headline: Formal coalition talks expected to start once the count is in
nz_politics.summary: ACT leader David Seymour has called for a single coalition agreement between National, ACT and NZ First rather than separate deals, and warned negotiations could run until Christmas. Prime Minister Christopher Luxon has said formal talks should wait for the official result, and candidates then have three working days to apply for recounts.
nz_politics.why: The length and shape of coalition talks will set when the new government's first economic decisions arrive.

world.headline: Iran widens its Hormuz shipping blacklist to tugboats
world.summary: Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority added 26 tugboats to its non-compliance list, which now covers 266 vessels that crossed the Strait of Hormuz without Tehran's permission. It has also warned companies that service tankers they could be listed, while a US naval blockade of Iranian ports continues.
world.why: Pressure on Gulf shipping is the main risk to oil and therefore to the fuel costs of running your work vehicle.

world.headline: Russian strikes hit Kyiv and Kharkiv as energy sites go offline
world.summary: Ballistic missiles struck Kyiv late on 25 November, injuring seven people, and a drone strike on a Kharkiv apartment block killed two. A thermal power plant and a gas facility halted operations, while Ukraine said it hit Russian refineries in Samara.
world.why: Attacks on energy infrastructure on both sides keep global fuel and gas markets jumpy, a live case study for your economics papers.

stories.headline: Retail sales post their biggest jump in almost five years
stories.summary: Stats NZ says retail sales volumes rose 2.2% in the September quarter, the strongest rise since late 2021, led by cars and parts, pharmacies and fuel. All 16 regions grew, and volumes were up 4.7% on a year earlier.
stories.why: Households spending again is a good sign for demand for home services like window and gutter cleaning heading into summer.

stories.headline: Markets lean towards an RBNZ rate rise as the Kiwi stays weak
stories.summary: Trading Economics reports markets have largely priced a 0.25 point OCR increase to 3.0% at the Reserve Bank's 9 December decision. The NZ dollar sits near 54.8 US cents after touching a 17-year low of 54.3 cents earlier this week.
stories.why: A rate rise would lift borrowing costs on business loans and vehicle finance, while a weak dollar makes imported equipment and supplies dearer.

marketing.headline: Brands turn TikTok creator videos into Meta ads
marketing.summary: Business Insider reports brands are re-running TikTok Shop creator videos as Meta ads, with one agency's clients logging 84,400 orders at a 4.3x return on ad spend over a month. TikTok Shop's US sales hit $969 million in the week to 22 November, up 57% on a year earlier.
marketing.why: One good short video of a job can do double duty: post it on TikTok or Reels, then reuse it as a paid Facebook ad instead of making new creative.

marketing.headline: Facebook ad costs climb into the holiday rush
marketing.summary: Meta's average price per ad rose 14% in the third quarter, and the US Facebook cost per thousand impressions averaged $21.45 in October, about 35% higher than a year earlier. Meta has also put its planned new self-serve ad terms on hold after legal and regulatory pushback.
marketing.why: With ad prices rising in peak season, tighter local targeting and strong creative matter more than ever to keep cost per booked quote down.

term.definition: How much revenue you earn for every dollar spent on advertising, calculated as sales from the ads divided by the ad cost. A ROAS of 4x means $4 of sales for each $1 spent, before other costs like labour and materials.
term.example: One agency says its clients earned a 4.3x return on ad spend by reusing TikTok creator videos as Meta ads, about $4.30 of sales for every $1 of ads.
